summary: The fix holds. composeSidebarTreeStructure now assigns threads in one O(T+W) pass using Map lookups on directory key, then linked node id. Path normalization is memoized, sortWorktrees runs once, and dedupe no longer calls JSON.stringify. A per-project cache shares one structure between Sidebar.visibleSidebarThreadKeys and SidebarProjectItem, which only decorates it. I copied the f1be4abc7 module out of git and benchmarked it against HEAD in Bun (JSC, not browser V8). Fixture: 30 projects, 30% of threads on unique worktree paths. At 2,000 threads the old composeSidebarTree took 8.0 ms and the new structure pass 0.82 ms (1.05 ms with decoration). At 8,000 threads it went from 109 ms to 3.9 ms, which scales linearly. With shared worktrees it went from 3.8 to 0.4 ms. Old and new trees came out identical on both fixtures. No other caller has a quadratic path: PhoneHome, useProjectMapCheckouts and the mobile app share the linear code or have no copy. What remains is optional, linear and small.

evidence.note: assignThreadsToWorktreeNodes buckets threads by Map lookup. Matching on directory key or linked node id is the same as the per-pair rules. A thread whose directory is not covered can only match nodes without a directory, so the per-pair belongsToWorktree fallback runs only over nodesWithoutDirectory, or over all nodes when the thread's key is null. That is effectively never, because project.cwd is the fallback.
Bounded memo for normalizeWorktreePath (4,096 entries, cleared when full).
The structure pass. sortWorktrees runs once (:212). Archived threads still go through synthesis, merge and assignment (:174, :194-210).

synthesizeWorktreeForThread sets archivedAt to null. A node synthesized only from archived threads therefore lands in the active worktrees list, so skipping archived threads would remove rows. That makes it a behaviour change, not a pure perf change.
One structure per project. Identity fast path first, then an element-wise fallback after merging drafts and sorting (sortThreadsWithPinned).
The Sidebar builds its own pinnedThreadKeys Set.
The project item builds a separate pinnedThreadKeys Set, so the two consumers never pass the same identity.

The Sidebar's per-project thread arrays come from groupByLogicalProjectKey and shareGroups. The item's come from selectSidebarThreadsForProjectRefs (SidebarProjectItem.tsx:121-129), a different array identity.

The item calls cache.structure() on every render, outside a memo, including for collapsed projects. SidebarWorktreeList still mounts with an empty visible set (SidebarProjectItem.tsx:515-517), while the Sidebar skips collapsed projects (Sidebar.tsx:1024).

A cache test covers a second consumer with its own arrays and its own pin Set getting the same structure. The useSidebarTree.test.ts:301 test is a fixture test, not an old-vs-new oracle. My ad-hoc parity run matched.

remaining: Nothing blocking. Optional, all linear: (1) Archived threads still go through the full structure pipeline (useSidebarTree.ts:174, 194-210). Benchmarked, deferring them would save about 0.4 ms at 2,000 threads. It would also drop worktree rows synthesized only from archived threads (useSidebarTree.ts:666-686, archivedAt null), so it is a behaviour change. (2) The Sidebar and SidebarProjectItem always pass different pinnedThreadKeys Sets and different thread-array identities. The identity fast path (sidebarProjectTreeCache.ts:75-84) therefore never serves the other consumer: each time the last caller switches, the cache merges drafts, re-sorts and runs sameElements before reusing the structure. That costs about 0.25 ms per call at 2,000 threads in one project, about a quarter of a rebuild. (3) SidebarProjectItem builds the structure for collapsed projects that show nothing (useSidebarProjectThreadPresentation.ts:153-160), so collapsed projects still pay one linear build at boot. (4) When a summary changes during streaming, that project's whole structure is rebuilt in O(T_p). Incremental reassignment is a separate topic.
fixDefects: No correctness defects found. Old and new trees came out identical on unique-path and shared-worktree fixtures, and the per-pair rule parity holds by inspection, duplicate node ids included. One correction to the auditor's minor point: the cross-consumer cache miss is not conditional ('if they hold different array identities'). It is structural and happens on every alternation (Sidebar.tsx:386 vs useSidebarProjectThreadPresentation.ts:45 for pins; Sidebar.tsx:770-777 vs SidebarProjectItem.tsx:121-129 for threads). The structure itself is still built once, so the cost is only the re-sort. The cache Maps (selectors, structures) are never pruned for removed projects, which is negligible retention.
implementationSketch: Optional, low priority. (a) Pass the Sidebar's pinnedThreadKeys Set to items through SidebarProjectTreeCacheContext, or memoize it from the uiState record inside the cache (e.g. cache.pinnedThreadKeys(record)). Then hold two entries per project in sidebarProjectTreeCache.structure, one per input identity: the latest Sidebar input and the latest item input, or a WeakMap from threads array to sortedThreads. Each consumer then hits its own identity fast path and the re-sort on alternation disappears. Test in sidebarVisibleThreadKeys.test.ts: alternate two consumers and assert sortThreadsWithPinned runs once, e.g. via a spy or counter. (b) In useSidebarProjectThreadPresentation, skip cache.structure() and return treeProject = null when !shouldShowThreadPanel. SidebarProjectItem would then render nothing for a collapsed project without a pinned thread; check that SidebarWorktreeList renders nothing in that case today. (c) Do not defer archived threads unless product accepts losing worktree rows synthesized only from archived threads. If they do, split archived threads out before ensureProjectWorktrees and compose them lazily when SidebarWorktreeList's archivedOpen becomes true.
decisionReason: Items (a) and (b) are internal caching changes with no behaviour change. Only the optional archived deferral (c) changes which rows are listed. It would need product sign-off and is not recommended.
correction: The auditor framed the cache re-sort on alternation as conditional. It always happens, because the Sidebar and the project item never share pinnedThreadKeys or thread-array identities. The cost is still small: about 0.25 ms per call at 2,000 threads in one project. The auditor also missed that the item builds structures for collapsed projects the Sidebar skips. Both are minor and do not change the DONE status.
